info.bio:
Jawbreaker es un grupo de música punk de San Francisco. Esta banda influyo mucho en la escena Punk Rock de Los Angeles.

El grupo tenía raíces en Los Ángeles, donde los integrantes Blake Schwarzenbach y Adam Pfahler, estudiaron en el Instituto Crossroads juntos, y también en Nueva York, donde Schwarzenbach y Pfahler conocieron al bajista Chris Bauermeister en la Universidad de Nueva York en 1988. El grupo se regía por la filosofía DIY, que pusieron en práctica al gestionarse ellos mismos sin necesidad de manager.

scenes.name: Hardcore en la era del punk-pop: emocore, ska-core y post-hardcore
scenes.author: Piero Scaruffi
scenes.desc: Mientras las revistas anuncian la «muerte del punk», el hardcore se convierte en un movimiento que no deja pueblo sin tocar y genera subgéneros. El «emocore» (Jawbreaker, Weezer, Sunny Day Real Estate, Promise Ring, At The Drive-In, Jimmy Eat World, Seaweed); el hardcore progresivo de Washington (Nation Of Ulysses, Make-Up, Shudder To Think, Jawbox, Edsel, Lungfish, Circus Lupus, Dismemberment Plan); el «ska-core» (Operation Ivy, Rancid, Mighty Mighty Bosstones, Sublime, No Doubt); el punk-pop que llega a las listas (Green Day, Offspring, Flop, Pennywise, Pegboy, Superchunk, Queers); el garage-punk californiano (Drive Like Jehu, Rocket From The Crypt, Blink 182, Zen Guerrilla); el jazzcore (Bazooka, Iceburn); la vieja escuela (D Generation, Supersuckers, Zeke, Dropkick Murphys, Silverfish, Turbonegro) y el post-hardcore de Unwound.

podcast.title: First Half 90s Emo Band
podcast.body: Jawbreaker is noted as an emo band from the first half of the 1990s, playing a role in the genre's formative years. "In the first half of the 90's, we had Sunday Day real estate and job breaker."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Journal-to-Songwriting Process
podcast.body: Singer Blake Schwarzenbach's creative process involved initially pouring his heart out into personal journals, then transforming those intimate thoughts and feelings into songs. This method created a profound connection with fans who deeply identified with his lyrics. "First, he poured his heart out into personal journals. Those thoughts and feelings were then turned into songs. And in the process, he achieved a really special connection with fans. They really, really identified with him."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

xref.title: Lyrical Source from Personal Journals
xref.body: As the singer for Jawbreaker, Blake Schwarzenbach developed a unique songwriting method: he first articulated his deepest thoughts and feelings in personal journals, which then became the raw material for his songs. This confessional approach forged a strong bond with the band's fanbase. "First, he poured his heart out into personal journals. Those thoughts and feelings were then turned into songs. And in the process, he achieved a really special connection with fans. They really, really identified with him."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
